author: ivanlitteri
content:
Ok, couldn't make up a reproducible setup. But the investigation resolved the following:
```
prysm-ethrex-2's beacon fell behind the chain for a few minutes. At its proposal slot (101721) its head was still the slot-101711 block, so it self-built and published a block extending a 9-slot-stale parent (exec block 99122) — while the canonical chain was already at exec block 99130. A block on a 9-slot-old parent can't win fork choice, so every node kept the heavier head and the block was orphaned on arrival. The payload itself was well-formed (timestamp correct for slot 101721); the only defect was the stale parent
```

content: The CPU usage was something that could've caused the beacon to fall behind
